transcript:
Header: 2026-08-25 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Ava, Diego, Priya, Sam, Jordan, Elena

Summary: quick practice session for SEs and PMM to tighten messaging vs competitors and run through demo flows. Filler / imperfect transcription present.

[00:00] Ava Chen: okay, um, thanks everyone for joining. quick housekeeping — we're doing a 45–60 minute run, we'll do two practice demos and then feedback.
[00:15] Diego Morales: hey! hi, uh, good morning everyone. i'll start the first demo, priya will jump in with the monitor, sam and jordan, you're our role players.
[00:30] Priya Kapoor: got it. i'm screen-sharing the demo deck now. (background chatter) sorry, little delay.
[00:45] Sam Li: looks good, yeah i can play product manager, ask about cold-start latency and data residency.
[01:05] Diego Morales: cool. opening line: "Redwood Inference gives you consistent latency across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments" — um, maybe we tighten that to "predictable latency and cost across deployment modes".
[01:20] Jordan Park: maybe call out SLA for dedicateds? sales people like numbers.
[01:35] Diego Morales: good call. i'll say: "dedicated capacity with SLA-backed latency targets".
[01:50] Priya Kapoor: (mumble) also note the quantization recommendation thing — we should say it reduces cost without big quality loss. sometimes folks interpret quant as major quality hit.
[02:05] Ava Chen: yes, messaging: "recommend quant profiles per workload; small quality delta but big cost upside".
[02:20] Sam Li: quick question: how do we position against Anthropic on safety? they always ask that.
[02:35] Diego Morales: yeah, uh, say we focus on production-grade reliability plus evals tied to prompt sets; not a safety-first marketing play, but we have quality monitoring and regressions alerts.
[02:50] Elena Rossi: call out our eval hooks in console — customers can pin prompts and get regression alerts.
[03:05] Jordan Park: okay practice demo start — open the app: "we'll show a live chat using a 13B LLM optimized on our runtime".
[03:20] Diego Morales: (typing) starts typing a prompt: "summarize last quarter's churn reasons" — demonstrating streaming and function calls.
[03:35] Priya Kapoor: small nit: in the flow mention prefix caching — customers like hearing about KV cache and batching. sometimes transcription will write KV as 'cash' ha.
[03:50] Diego Morales: right. "we autoprefix cache popular prompts which reduces tokens by up to 30% in many workloads" — is that claim ok?
[04:05] Sam Li: that sounds like an anecdote, we've got a benchmark slide that shows 20–40% in customer A. be careful with exact % unless it's cited.
[04:20] Diego Morales: yep, i'll say "often 20–40% depending on workload".
[04:35] Priya Kapoor: demo glitch: streaming didn't show chunked outputs quickly, we should call out network and model choices.
[04:50] Ava Chen: mention smart routing fallback — if the hosted model hits capacity, we fallback to a compatible variant with slightly different latency/cost.
[05:05] Diego Morales: (mumbles) fallback — good for uptime. also talk about dedicated burst capacity for spikes.
[05:20] Sam Li: objection rehearsal: customer asks "but OpenAI has better models" — how do we respond?
[05:35] Diego Morales: two angles: 1) model parity for many workloads with curated open models + Redwood-verified perf; 2) serving economics + routing and private options — those are business wins.
[05:50] Jordan Park: add third: observability and rollouts — canary, A/B, tracing. engineers care.
[06:05] Priya Kapoor: experiment: i'll play an infra engineer, ask about VPC/private deployments and key management.
[06:20] Ava Chen: good — demo: "we offer private control plane, VPC peering, KMS integrations and audit logs for regulated workloads".
[06:35] Elena Rossi: question: we should be ready to mention SOC 2 / ISO if asked.
[06:50] Diego Morales: yes, keep a slide handy: SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC.
[07:05] Sam Li: objection: "latency too high for real-time agents" — how do we handle?
[07:20] Diego Morales: mention sequence-length aware kernel selection, continuous batching, and attention optimizations — we reduce per-token latency and cost. give a concrete: median p99 for this model on our runtime is X ms — (note: X replaced during live demos with slide number).
[07:40] Priya Kapoor: minor stumble: we sometimes say 'KV cache management' then 'prefix cache' interchangeably enough to confuse. pick one.
[07:55] Ava Chen: agreed; stick to 'KV cache' in technical convos, 'prefix caching' in biz convos.
[08:10] Diego Morales: demo step two: show model switch: route a request to a quantized variant to show cost drop. (demo fumbling) hmm audio lag.
[08:25] Priya Kapoor: typo in the script: "quant profiles by workload" is good, but include a one-liner: "quantization reduces compute by x2–4 with minimal quality regression" — again cite if possible.
[08:40] Sam Li: we'll add slide with real numbers from optimize toolkit later.
[08:55] Jordan Park: roleplay: customer asks about governance and audit logs retention.
[09:10] Ava Chen: respond: "we support configurable retention, audit trails, and KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments".
[09:25] Diego Morales: feedback: you said 'we're flexible' — be specific: "configurable retention up to N days/months (depending on contract)". avoid getting into legal specifics.
[09:40] Priya Kapoor: (interrupt) crosstalk — in demo mention 'auto-batching' and show a graph.
[09:55] Diego Morales: ok pulling up the perf slide — shows batching throughput curves.
[10:10] Sam Li: quick training note: SEs should memorize two or three crisp customer stories about cost reduction and reliability; those land better than abstract claims.
[10:25] Ava Chen: agree. one-liner examples: "Customer X reduced token spend by 35% via caching and quant".
[10:40] Elena Rossi: practice safety question again: how do we compare to Anthropic — technical answer then high-level.
[10:55] Diego Morales: technical: Anthropic has model safety focus; we emphasize serving and deployment flexibility. high-level: "they have strengths; we win on economics and ops".
[11:10] Priya Kapoor: demo glitch highlights — make a note to smooth the 'switch model' script step; it looked janky.
[11:25] Ava Chen: capturing that. action: Diego revise switch flow.
[11:40] (Time jump) [20:00] Diego Morales: starting second practice run — i'm tightening phrasing, starting with customer pain: "we can't get consistent latency across regions".
[20:15] Sam Li: customer: "we need data residency and private control plane".
[20:30] Diego Morales: reply includes details on VPC/on-prem option and KMS, mention audit logs.
[20:45] Priya Kapoor: nice — this time the streaming output showed chunked results faster.
[21:00] Jordan Park: cue for cost objection: "we're concerned about per-token costs".
[21:15] Diego Morales: response: "we expose batching, caching, and quantization levers; Redwood Optimize recommends profiles to reduce unit cost while preserving quality".
[21:30] Sam Li: roleplay push: "what's your migration path from OpenAI?"
[21:45] Diego Morales: say: "we support model mapping and routing, and provide migration playbooks and eval harnesses to ensure parity".
[22:00] Ava Chen: add note: include migration checklist in SE deck.
[22:15] Priya Kapoor: feedback from Jordan: be more concise in the opening minute; customers tune out long context.
[22:30] Diego Morales: ok will shorten intro to 30s elevator: problem, what we do, brief demo.
[22:45] Sam Li: also include one-slide competitive grid with quick bullets: latency, cost, private options, observability.
[23:00] Diego Morales: (reading) "competitive grid — OpenAI: strong model quality, less control; Anthropic: safety; Cohere: embeddings; Redwood: serving economics, private deployments, observability." 
[23:20] Priya Kapoor: small mispronunciation: sometimes we say 'Re-plicate' wrong.
[23:35] Ava Chen: haha noted.
[23:50] (Feedback round) [30:00] Jordan Park: Diego, strong demo energy, but slow transitions; cut by 20% and it will feel tighter.
[30:15] Sam Li: keep the story about caching early — it's a differentiator.
[30:30] Priya Kapoor: add slide that shows cost/latency tradeoff curve with quant profiles.
[30:45] Diego Morales: i'll annotate the slide with callouts: where to pivot to dedicated vs hosted.
[31:00] Ava Chen: roleplay objection: "We have compliance needs — can we run on-prem?"
[31:15] Diego Morales: "yes, private deployments with optional on-prem packages; plus KMS/HSM and audit logs".
[31:30] Elena Rossi: ask: do we support SSO and SCIM?
[31:45] Priya Kapoor: quick answer: SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning supported; mention RBAC.
[32:00] Jordan Park: training tip: have a tiny cheat sheet of admin settings and links.
[32:15] Diego Morales: agreed.
[32:30] (Demo hiccup) [35:00] Diego Morales: the quantified example didn't show latency numbers; i'll fudge with slide references, but we should update demo env to surface p99 numbers.
[35:20] Ava Chen: action: Priya to capture exact numbers and add to demo env by next practice.
[35:35] Priya Kapoor: will do.
[35:50] Sam Li: let's practice the closing: next steps — pilots, benchmarks, and security review.
[36:05] Diego Morales: close: "we'll follow up with pricing, security docs, and a simple POC template".
[36:20] Jordan Park: good.
[36:35] (Quick Q/A) [40:00] Elena Rossi: competition nuance: how to position vs NVIDIA inference solutions?
[40:15] Diego Morales: say: "NVIDIA offers hardware and inferencing stack; Redwood offers a unified runtime and routing across hardware and models — we integrate with cloud infra but provide dev experience." 
[40:30] Ava Chen: mention partnerships and marketplace presence for credibility.
[40:45] Sam Li: training note: include a line in battlecard: "when customer asks about NVIDIA, pivot to infra+software value".
[41:00] Priya Kapoor: wrap-up practice: we did two runs, captured snags: model switch, missing p99 numbers, tighten intro.
[41:15] Diego Morales: agreed.
[41:30] Ava Chen: recap of next steps: update battlecard, update demo env, schedule follow-up practice.
[41:45] Jordan Park: i'll book the follow-up for 2026-09-02 10:00AM PT.
[42:00] Sam Li: i'll prepare the competitive one-pager for OpenAI/Anthropic by 2026-08-31.
[42:15] Priya Kapoor: i'll record the intro video and update slide by 2026-09-03.
[42:30] Diego Morales: i'll push demo script updates to the shared repo and link in the SE kit.
[42:45] Ava Chen: perfect. any final Qs?
[43:00] (silence / small chats)
[43:15] Jordan Park: thanks everyone.
[43:30] Ava Chen: thanks team, see you at follow-up.
[43:45] (meeting end)

Notes: Transcript contains imperfect transcriptions (misheard product names, occasional 'KV cash' etc.) — left as-is to reflect typical Fireflies export. References: demo deck (internal link), competitive battlecard (internal link), demo-env showing p99 numbers (to be updated).
